comparison: Perfect alignment on chromatin accessibility validation (C13-C18). Both evaluations support the claims with OpenEval providing detailed quantitative assessment (80% overlap, sensitivity/specificity metrics) while peer reviewers acknowledge good QC metrics and benchmark analyses without raising concerns.

Strong alignment on oCGI analysis (C44-C52). Both evaluations support these findings. OpenEval provides detailed assessment of spatial associations, methylation patterns, and interaction preferences. Peer reviewers implicitly support through recognition of integrated multi-omic capabilities and convincing data, with no specific concerns raised.

Strong alignment on methylation calling validation (C8-C12). Both evaluations support the claims. OpenEval details WGBS validation, statistical significance, and AUC values. Peer reviewers explicitly state QC metrics are good and data is convincing, with C32 addressed separately in peer R6.

Strong alignment on practical specifications (C59, C60, C62). Both evaluations support these claims. OpenEval characterizes them as factual statements about method characteristics. Peer reviewers acknowledge practical utility and accept method as valuable addition despite stated limitations. C61 addressed in peer R9 but not OpenEval R11.

Strong alignment on spatial heterogeneity of chromatin accessibility (C33-C39). Both evaluations support these novel findings. OpenEval provides detailed assessment of quantitative data and biological validation. Peer reviewers support through statement that conclusions are backed by convincing data and recognition of multi-omic integration capabilities. C40-C42 included in peer R7 but addressed separately in OpenEval R8.

Strong alignment on technical optimization (C5-C7). Both evaluations support these claims. OpenEval details gel electrophoresis validation and enzyme choice rationale. Peer reviewers implicitly accept through statements about convincing data and good QC metrics. OpenEval R1 also covers C1-C2 which peer reviewers address in R1.

Moderate alignment on 3D genome capabilities. OpenEval R2 addresses high-order chromatin interactions (C3-C4, C19-C24) while peer R5 covers broader 3D genome validation (C19-C28). Both support the claims. OpenEval provides detailed quantitative assessment while peer reviewers acknowledge good benchmark analyses and QC metrics.

Alignment on transcription factor footprints and CTCF binding (C30-C31). Both evaluations support these claims. OpenEval details footprint detection validation and relationship to chromatin structure. Peer reviewers implicitly support through acceptance of convincing data. Peer R6 also includes C29 and C32 which OpenEval addresses in R5 and R3 respectively.

Partial alignment on chromatin conformation validation. Both address C25-C28 and support the claims. OpenEval R5 also covers C61 (addressed in peer R9) and provides detailed assessment of reproducibility and Hi-C correlations. Peer R5 also covers C19-C24 (addressed in OpenEval R2) and acknowledges good benchmark analyses.

Partial alignment on enhancer-promoter regulation (C40-C42). Both evaluations support these claims. OpenEval provides detailed assessment of quantitative breakdown and correlation with gene expression. Peer R7 primarily focuses on C33-C39 (spatial heterogeneity) but encompasses C40-C42 through statement about convincing data supporting conclusions.

Partial alignment on methodological foundation. Both address C1-C2 and support the claims. OpenEval R1 covers broader technical validation (C1-C2, C5-C7) with detailed enzyme comparison data. Peer R1 focuses on overall methodological advance (C1-C4) and recognizes SCA-seq as valuable tool, with C3-C4 addressed in OpenEval R2.

Minimal overlap on methodological claims. OpenEval R2 addresses high-order chromatin interactions (C3-C4, C19-C24) while peer R1 focuses on overall methodological advance (C1-C4). Both support C3-C4. OpenEval provides detailed quantitative validation while peer reviewers provide broad endorsement of method as valuable advance.

OpenEval R10 addresses background knowledge and literature context (C53-C58). These are established concepts cited to motivate SCA-seq development. No corresponding peer review evaluation found as these represent background rather than novel findings requiring validation.
